title: ByteSmith Labs
text:
ByteSmith Labs

notes:
Lead source: self-serve signup + inbound form. Founders ex-GitHub, building an in-IDE code assistant and codebase search with long-context support. Wants hosted API to avoid infra ops. Primary asks: reliable long context (>=64k tokens), streaming partial tokens to client (TypeScript SDK), per-route rate limits and burst handling, predictable token pricing for budgeting.

Conversation highlights: 
- 2026-03-09 call w/ Aisha + Marco. CTO (Jared) said: "We need context window for whole repo + cross-file nav, otherwise suggestions are useless."
- They ran basic eval on open models; saw parity on small prompts but performance degrades on 16k+ contexts. Asking for performance profile (latency vs tokens) of hosted models.
- Very cost-sensitive: startup runway 18 months, wants to cap monthly token spend; interested in volume discounts/commit tiers if predictable.
- SDK request: first-class TS streaming + reconnect/resume semantics, backpressure controls, and example Vite/VSCode extension snippet.
- Security: SOC2 + SSO required for any paid plan; prefer data processed in AWS us-east-1.

Quote: "If we can get 64k streaming with sub-1s initial-token latency and stable pricing, we can move from eval to paid within 4–6 weeks."

Internal notes: they created 3 sandbox API keys from self-serve, hit 429s when simulating multi-dev usage — likely need clearer rate-limit guidance and soft-quota for POCs. Shared Redwood quickstart link and pricing deck. Need to provide short PoC runbook and transient higher RPS for demo day.

next_step:
Technical demo + latency/cost PoC on hosted API (3/17) — provide transient API key + example TS SDK snippet for streaming

blockers:
rate_limit_clarity
cost_per_token unknown for long context
SDK streaming reliability
